applies_why: The judge text decides D5 vs C5 by weighing multiple cited verses or chains, not by treating a single verse's silence as a ground for UNDERDETERMINED.
quote: D5 vs C5 (Isaiah 7:14): UNDERDETERMINED -- the sign's chapter bounds (Isaiah 7:16; 8:3-4; 8:8) are real, but C5's own narrowing concedes Matthew 1:23's application stands, and the almah/bethulah word-count cuts both ways (Joel 1:8); answered in [CR2] section G and [CR3] LINK 5.
rule_words: That a single verse does not state a link or its contrary is never a ground for STANDS or UNDERDETERMINED, for either side. A verse that carries two senses at once is not open. Both senses stand. This is about one verse. It does not apply when the judge weighs two chains.
room: Phrase: It does not apply when the judge weighs two chains. I read the cited Isaiah 7:16/8:3-4/8:8 bounds against Matthew 1:23 and the Joel 1:8 word-count as two chains, so K-S2 is inapplicable; the opposing reading treats the word-count line as a single-verse ambiguity that K-S2 would govern.
why: Because the rule expressly does not apply when the judge weighs two chains, and the text weighs the Isaiah 7:16/8:3-4/8:8 bounds against Matthew 1:23 and the almah/bethulah word-count, the text is CLEAN under K-S2.
